name: Ilish Bhapa
subtitle: hilsa steamed in raw mustard paste and mustard oil, sharp and unapologetic

ingredients.note: rohu works, but ilish is the point of the dish
soaked, then ground with the soaking water

ingredients.qty: 6, four for the paste and two whole

ingredients.note: keeps the mustard from turning harsh
some homes add it, some do not

ingredients.qty: 3 tbsp for the paste, plus water for the steamer

prepNotes: Soak the mustard seeds for 20 minutes in warm water with one green chilli and a good pinch of salt, then grind to a fine paste with 3 tbsp of that water. Grinding mustard dry, or grinding it too long, makes it bitter.
Rinse the hilsa once and pat it dry. Do not wash it under running water for long, and do not scale it hard: its oil is its flavour.
Rub the fish with the turmeric and salt and leave it 15 minutes while you set up the steamer.
You need a tight-lidded steel tiffin box or a heatproof bowl with foil, sitting in a covered pan of simmering water.

steps.text: Grind the soaked mustard seeds with four green chillies, the sugar and 3 tbsp of the soaking water to a smooth, pourable paste.
steps.tip: Strain the paste through a coarse sieve if you dislike the husk; it costs you nothing in flavour.

steps.text: Mix the paste with the coconut, 4 tbsp of the mustard oil, the remaining turmeric and salt to taste.
Turn the fish pieces gently in this mixture until each is fully coated, and let them sit 10 minutes.
Lay the fish in a single layer in the tiffin box, pour over any leftover paste and tuck in the two whole green chillies.
steps.tip: A single layer only. Stacked pieces steam unevenly and the bottom ones overcook.

steps.text: Spoon the last tablespoon of raw mustard oil over the top and close the lid tightly.
Set the box in a pan with water coming a third of the way up its sides, cover the pan, and steam on medium for 20 to 22 minutes.
steps.tip: Keep the water at a steady simmer, not a rolling boil, which rattles the box and breaks the fish.

steps.text: Turn off the heat and leave the box closed for a further 5 minutes.
Open carefully, away from your face, and serve with hot plain rice, spooning the mustard oil from the box over each portion.

storage: Eat the same day. It keeps 24 hours refrigerated but the mustard sharpens overnight; reheat by steaming the closed box again for 5 minutes rather than in a pan.
